rationale:
ROUND 9 of 7ba5b8c4 — the one objection that stopped round 8 is now CLOSED IN
PRODUCTION, by a separate change that was reviewed and shipped on its own merits.

ROUND 8 WAS 8 APPROVE / 1 OBJECT. The single objection (diagnosis_guardian, medium)
was CORRECT and was mine: admitting kind='doc' would let a markdown excerpt satisfy
the STATIC tier of a CONFIRMED verdict -- the tier that means "code was read" --
because pkg/diagnose/loop.go:60 defines TierStatic AS this table, step.go:145 gates
CONFIRMED on it, and the assembler printed the literal words "They are CODE" over
everything the index returned.

I DID NOT ANSWER IT IN THIS PLAN, AND THAT IS THE SUBSTANTIVE POINT OF ROUND 9.
Three things followed instead:

(1) IT WAS NOT SPLIT OUT AS A BUG. Round 7 legitimately split the prune floor into
bugs_open/135 because that defect exists TODAY with or without markdown -- someone
else's, surfaced by my call site. THIS hazard does not exist until this plan ships.
Filing a bug for a defect your own unshipped change creates, then shipping the
change, is not a split; it is shipping a known defect with a paper trail.

(2) IT WENT TO THE OWNER, because it is a design question about what an evidence
tier MEANS, with four options at different costs. OWNER RULING 2026-07-29: option
1b. Recorded in DECISIONS_open_for_owner_2026-07-26_architecture_seat.md section D12,
which also records the option that was measured and rejected: excluding doc rows
from diagnose_code_lookup would have made the corpus invisible to feature-designer,
which is where review_architecture sits -- i.e. it would have blinded the seat this
corpus exists to equip.

(3) THE GUARD SHIPPED FIRST, ALONE, ON ITS OWN CORRELATION. Not folded in here.
It alters a shared mechanism -- the evidence labelling of every diagnosis run -- and
the 2026-07-28 seam ruling routes such a change to review on its own merits rather
than letting it ride inside a feature plan. Folding it in would also have repeated
rounds 4-6 exactly: answer an objection by adding mechanism INSIDE the plan, and
watch the mechanism become the next argument.

**SO THE HAZARD IS ALREADY CLOSED, AND NOT BY AN ARGUMENT IN THIS DOCUMENT.**
corr da1f9c81-0b4b-41ff-9b2c-bc0057ad3cf8 -- APPROVED by 12 reviewers, 0 unreadable,
with diagnosis_guardian (the seat that RAISED the objection) approving at zero
objections. Built, rolled and pod-verified LIVE on chassis v1.0.1200 on BOTH replicas:
"They are CODE" 1 -> 0 (the string the change DELETES), docTag 0 -> 1,
answerCodeCheck = 10 as positive control. So when this plan's markdown rows arrive,
answerCodeCheck ALREADY tags any non-code row [doc], groups them under a prose
sub-heading, and the bundle heading ALREADY tells the verdicter prose is not
static-tier evidence. **The guard preceded the corpus, which is the ordering the
seam ruling asks for and which shipping them together would not have given.**

WHAT CHANGED IN THIS PLAN, three things, all small:

- **MIGRATION RENUMBERED 254 -> 267, and this is not bookkeeping.** The round-8 plan
  said "253 is highest today -- re-read the max immediately before writing the file."
  I re-read it: the highest on disk is now **266**. 254 has been taken by another
  session since round 1. This is the third time this workstream's migration number
  has moved under it.
- **A defensive ROLLBACK; preamble before BEGIN;** -- conceding debug_historian
  (low, round 8): an aborted transaction from a prior failed run in the same psql
  session is sticky, and the idempotent pg_constraint check does not help if the
  session is already poisoned.
- **The VERIFY gains a NEGATIVE CONTROL** -- conceding the architecture seat (low,
  on the guard's own review): a presence check passes if ONE doc row is tagged; the
  negative control is what fails if any row is MISSED, which is the failure the
  guard exists to stop. That seat asked for it "while the seam is fresh" and this is
  the plan it was asking of.
- **kindDoc is NO LONGER DECLARED HERE.** The guard already declares it live
  (diagnose_code_lookup_action.go), along with codeKindList/codeKinds/docTag/isCode.
  Re-declaring it would not compile. This is the ordinary cost of splitting a change
  in two and is stated so the implementer does not reintroduce it.

FIGURES RE-MEASURED THIS ROUND RATHER THAN CARRIED, because round 8 carried one and
it was wrong: code_symbols is **5,017 rows / 5,017 bodies / 0 markdown / 5 kinds**
today -- NOT the 4,992 round 8's grounded_in stated, which was already stale when I
submitted it. The sizing ratio (~3,472 doc sections against ~5,000 code rows, ~+69%)
is unchanged at this precision.

CARRIED FORWARD, unchanged and previously checked: docs/ is on disk
(github_source.go:196-245 writes every tar entry, no path filter; the
analyse_repo_local_action.go:285 exclude is analyser-time) and out.Root survives
collected_data; the register glob is register/*.md (110 entries), not the parent
(28 superseded planning docs) -- round 1's real defect; no markdown splitter exists
to reuse. THE PRUNE remains out of scope and filed as bugs_open/135, unowned;
prune behaviour after this plan is exactly what it is today.

plan.summary: ROUND 9. D11 layer 1b: relax the kind CHECK and index markdown sections from four durable prose sources into code_symbols. Round 8's single objection -- that a doc row could satisfy the STATIC tier of a CONFIRMED verdict -- was correct, went to the owner as decision D12, was ruled option 1b, and the guard has since been REVIEWED SEPARATELY (corr da1f9c81, APPROVED 12-0) and SHIPPED LIVE on v1.0.1200, pod-verified on both replicas. The hazard is closed before the corpus arrives. This round adds no mechanism: a renumbered migration (254->267, the number moved again), a defensive ROLLBACK preamble, and a negative control in the VERIFY.

edits.rationale: code_symbols.kind carries a CHECK permitting Go kinds ONLY, so a markdown row cannot be inserted at all -- the mechanical blocker. Verbatim from the live DB: CHECK ((kind = ANY (ARRAY['func'::text, 'method'::text, 'struct'::text, 'interface'::text, 'alias'::text, 'type'::text, 'var'::text, 'const'::text]))). Adds 'doc'. READERS enumerated for guardian, and RE-MEASURED IN ROUND 8 against its objection that this claim is one its own tier cannot verify (code_checks see declarations, never switch bodies): seven live read sites, NONE selecting kind; the column reaches Go only at code_symbols_actions.go:528 and :549, both -> scanCodeSymbolRows:566-585, which scans it into a result map and never compares it. Four branch sites on a variable NAMED kind exist and none is the column (three are the code_check kind namespace, one is the analyser's typeDef.Kind on the write path) -- ROUNDS 6-7 SAID 'ONE HIT' AND THAT COUNT WAS WRONG. Full census with column lists and file:line in grounded_in. NUMBER MOVED AGAIN, and I re-read it rather than trusting round 8: the highest on disk is now **266**, so this is 267. Round 8 said 253; before that this workstream was approved as 241 and shipped as 243 because two sessions took 241/242 inside four hours. THIRD time the number has moved under this plan -- re-read `ls` immediately before writing the file, never a handoff.

ROUND 2, answering debug_historian (medium): the needle-gate discipline wants verify AND rollback as separate files, and this constraint relaxation is what makes the Go writer's INSERTs possible at all -- so a bad flattenMarkdown run had no scripted recovery. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS FILE IS NOT TRIVIAL: the old CHECK cannot be restored while kind='doc' rows exist, so the rows must be deleted FIRST or the ALTER fails with a check-violation on existing data. Written as one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable.

ROUND 9: **`kindDoc` IS ALREADY DECLARED LIVE** by the D12 guard (corr da1f9c81, chassis v1.0.1200) in diagnose_code_lookup_action.go, together with codeKindList/codeKinds/docTag/isCode. Re-declaring it here would not compile. That is the ordinary cost of shipping the guard first and is stated so the implementer does not reintroduce it. ROUND 3, rewritten for bug_historian (medium): the round-2 guard fired only on a TOTAL of zero, and round 1's real defect was non-zero-but-wrong-source. Now: counts are tracked PER GLOB and returned; a glob matching ZERO FILES is a hard error (the plan's only fail-loud escalation, because a source contributing nothing is indistinguishable from a source that does not exist); and the scope/path-shape assertion runs HERE, every index, not only in a VERIFY a human runs once. NOT REUSING, with the search attached in the rationale: chunkContent (rag_actions.go:396) is a fixed-width window; extractProductSection (vet_med_price_scrape_action.go:650) is markdown- and heading-aware but TRUNCATES at a fixed end-marker list and returns one prefix with no spans; no markdown parser is a dependency (goldmark is go.sum-graph-only, absent from go.mod, imported nowhere). Suffix determinism, for guardian (low): the counter is a per-file map[string]int incremented during ONE top-to-bottom pass over the file's own lines, so the Nth occurrence gets the same suffix every run -- document order, never map iteration order.

content does THREE jobs -- trigram text, the EMBEDDED text, and the input to content_hash which is the re-embed trigger. composeSymbolContent keeps the code BODY out for exactly this reason; markdown must obey the same rule or the first reindex re-embeds all 4,992 existing rows plus the new ones. So content is heading + path only; the section text goes to body, which is what the content check now searches anyway.

ROUND 7: append markdown rows to the Go rows before the EXISTING upsert/prune loop, which is UNCHANGED by this plan. Round 4-6's prune floor is removed and filed as bugs_open/135 -- it guards a pre-existing exposure on the code rows that exists with or without this change, and iterating it here was spending council rounds on a different change. Prune behaviour after this plan is exactly what it is today. THE GLOBS ARE THE DESIGN and round 1 got one wrong: the register is register/*.md (110 entries), not the parent (28 superseded planning docs). Owning pipeline, NOW A QUERY RESULT rather than prose (prior_art_librarian + guardian, round 7 -- it was the only prose-only claim in the submission): agent_definitions holds EXACTLY ONE wiring of index_code_symbols, code-indexer/index_symbols, so single-pipeline ownership of the write path is settled from the DB side; scheduled_tasks holds code-index-refresh -> index-orchestrator, 86400s, enabled, last fired 2026-07-28 12:46:27Z. Both queries and both results in grounded_in.

ROUND 8, answering debug_historian (medium): this file's assertions were ALL DB-only, and that is a named gap on this platform, not a hypothetical one. The sharper form of the objection: every assertion below would read IDENTICALLY against a pod that never received the code -- kind='doc' rows would simply be absent, which is indistinguishable from 'the roll has not happened yet'. Step 0 closes that, and it is discriminating rather than decorative because the pre-roll baseline is MEASURED. A SUPPLEMENT, not a fix -- explicitly conceding editquality (low, edit 6): this file changes no behaviour and is not counted as covering any mechanism. It exists because 243's VERIFY caught a real defect in layer 1 that a reviewer had been asked to eyeball. Carries the 243 lesson forward: that file's EXPLAIN stayed pinned to the OLD predicate after the code changed, so it reported on a query nobody ran while presenting as coverage -- these assertions must be re-read whenever flattenMarkdown or the globs change.

--    DB-only and would read the SAME against a pod that never got the code:
--    kind='doc' rows would just be absent, which is indistinguishable from
--    "the roll has not happened yet". So prove the deploy at the RUNNING POD --
--    never git, never the image tag (a same-tag rebuild ships the node's stale
--    cached binary; 1188/1189 shared one image id built 56 min BEFORE the fix
--    it was supposed to carry).
--      POD=$(kubectl -n ai-persona-system get pods -l app=agent-chassis \
--            -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
--      kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec $POD -- sh -c \
--        'strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c flattenMarkdown'        -- want > 0
--      kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec $POD -- sh -c \
--        'strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c composeSymbolContent'   -- want > 0
--    MEASURED PRE-ROLL BASELINE, 2026-07-28, agent-chassis-74dbd9c9f4-7p6d8:
--      flattenMarkdown 0 · composeDocContent 0 · defaultDocGlobs 0   <- the change
--      composeSymbolContent 2 · scanCodeSymbolRows 2                 <- POSITIVE
--      CONTROL: existing symbols present, so a 0 above is a real absence and not
--      a broken grep against a stripped or renamed binary.
--    A 0 for flattenMarkdown AFTER the roll means THE IMAGE DID NOT SHIP THE
--    CHANGE, not that markdown indexing failed. Re-grep after any roll you did
--    not perform yourself.
-- 1. the layer-1 invariant must survive across ALL rows, not just new ones
SELECT count(*) AS hash_drift FROM code_symbols
 WHERE content_hash IS DISTINCT FROM encode(sha256(convert_to(content,'UTF8')),'hex');  -- 0
-- 2. markdown arrived, and ONLY from the four sources (the scope guard)
SELECT kind, count(*) FROM code_symbols GROUP BY 1;              -- expect a 'doc' row
SELECT count(*) AS out_of_scope FROM code_symbols WHERE kind='doc'
 AND path NOT LIKE 'bugs_open/%' AND path NOT LIKE 'bugs_closed/%'
 AND path NOT LIKE '%WRONG_CALLS.md' AND path NOT LIKE '%016b_%'
 AND path NOT LIKE 'docs/agent_docs/docs026_concept_register/register/%';   -- 0
-- 2b. and the register half that round 1 would have MISSED is present
SELECT count(*) AS register_sections FROM code_symbols
 WHERE kind='doc' AND path LIKE '%docs026_concept_register/register/%';     -- > 0
-- 3. a prose-only string is findable (it is not in any .go file)
SELECT count(*) AS wrongcalls_hits FROM code_symbols
 WHERE kind='doc' AND body ILIKE '%wrote-it-down-before-i-checked-it%';     -- > 0
SELECT count(*) AS negative_control FROM code_symbols
 WHERE body ILIKE '%zzz_string_that_appears_nowhere_zzz%';                  -- 0
-- 4. collisions did not silently swallow sections
-- 4. section count, MECHANICALLY DERIVED at verify time, not remembered.
--    (debug_historian, round 4: a remembered figure caught my own stale ~1,749,
--     measured before the register glob was fixed. Real figure: ~3,472.)
--    Expected, computed from the checkout the indexer used:
--      { grep -h '^#\{2,3\} ' WRONG_CALLS 016b; cat bugs_*/*.md | grep '^## ';
--        cat docs026_concept_register/register/*.md | grep '^#\{2,3\} '; } | wc -l
SELECT count(*) AS sections FROM code_symbols WHERE kind='doc';
SELECT path, count(*) FROM code_symbols WHERE kind='doc' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10;
-- ══ ROUND 9 — THE NEGATIVE CONTROL (architecture seat, low, on corr da1f9c81) ══
-- Everything above is a PRESENCE check: it passes if doc rows arrive and one is
-- tagged. The seat's point is that presence cannot fail in the direction that
-- matters. What must fail is a doc row rendering AS CODE. So, after the first
-- index that includes markdown, in a REAL diagnosis bundle:
--
--   1. every rendered line whose path is a doc glob MUST carry the [doc] tag
--        -> expect 0 exceptions
--   2. every such line MUST fall AFTER the prose sub-heading, never among the
--      code rows
--        -> expect 0 exceptions
--   3. and the inverse, which is the one a presence check can never catch:
--      NO row with a .go path may carry [doc]
--        -> expect 0 exceptions
--
-- The guard is an ALLOW-LIST (codeKinds), so an unknown future kind renders as
-- NOT-code. Check 3 is what detects the opposite mistake -- a Go kind wrongly
-- omitted from that list, which would silently demote real code out of the
-- static tier and quietly weaken every CONFIRMED verdict.
SELECT count(*) AS doc_rows FROM code_symbols WHERE kind='doc';        -- > 0 by now
SELECT count(*) AS go_rows_untagged FROM code_symbols
 WHERE kind <> 'doc' AND path LIKE '%.go';                             -- the population check 3 covers

plan.risks: (1) THE ONE INVARIANT: content and content_hash must not gain section text or every existing row re-embeds. composeDocContent is heading+path only; the VERIFY asserts hash integrity across ALL rows. (2) EMBEDDING COST: ~3,472 new rows each embed once on first index. Layer 1's cost was zero-by-construction; this is not, and it is stated. (3) IDENTITY COLLISION: in-file duplicate headings measured at 1 today (WRONG_CALLS.md 212 headings / 211 unique); the suffix counter runs in document order over one top-to-bottom pass, so it is stable across runs. (4) SCOPE IS THE DESIGN AND ROUND 1 GOT IT WRONG ONCE: the register glob pointed at 28 superseded planning docs instead of 110 register entries -- a wrong glob poisons the corpus with the stale-doc class this plan exists to keep out, while every counter reports success. Per-glob counts, a zero-match glob failing the doc half, and the VERIFY's out-of-scope + register_sections assertions are the guards. (5) BLAST RADIUS of the CHECK widening, enumerated and re-checked: no reader switches on kind; the only behavioural change is that a doc row can appear in lookup_code_symbols' top-k, which is the intended effect. (6) PRUNE: unchanged by this plan. The pre-existing no-floor exposure is bugs_open/135. (7) DEPLOY: Go is inert until the image rolls; the CHECK relaxes immediately and markdown simply does not arrive until then -- a degrade, not a break. HOW THE ROLL IS CONFIRMED (debug_historian, round 7 -- the plan previously said Go was inert but never said how it would know the roll happened): no doc_sections count is trusted until the RUNNING pod's binary greps non-zero for flattenMarkdown, read against the measured pre-roll baseline of 0 with composeSymbolContent=2 as the positive control. VERIFY step 0. Neither git nor the image tag is evidence.
